sDescription: Kendrick Lamar was at No.1 on the UK chart with his sixth studio album GNX, Lamar's second No.1 album on the UK Albums Chart after To Pimp a Butterfly (2015). GNX earned over 44.2 million first-day streams on the global Spotify chart, averaging over 3.6 million streams per song despite being available only seven hours prior. In the United States, GNX debuted atop the Billboard 200 with 319,000 album-equivalent units, including 379.72 million official on-demand streams.

American musician and songwriter, Irving Burgie regarded as one of the greatest composers of Caribbean music died aged 95. He composed 34 songs for Harry Belafonte, including eight of the 11 songs on the Belafonte album Calypso (1956), the first album of any kind to sell one million copies. He was inducted into the Songwriters Hall of Fame in 2007.

Dick Dodd, drummer and vocalist for The Standells on their 1966 hit 'Dirty Water', died of cancer at the age of 68. 'Dirty Water' became an anthem for sports fans in Boston with its refrain of "Boston, you're my home," despite the group having no direct connection with the city.

Susan Boyle's album became the best-selling debut in UK chart history when it went to No.1 on the UK chart. The 48 year-old runner-up in ITV's Britain's Got Talent, sold 410,000 copies of ‘I Dreamed a Dream’. Boyle also topped the US charts, setting a first-week sales record for a female debut album with 701,000 copies sold in its first week.

Former Lynyrd Skynyrd drummer Artimus Pyle, a convicted sex offender, was arrested for failing to properly register a new permanent address. The 59-year-old had pleaded guilty in 1993 to charges of attempted capital sexual battery by an adult on a victim younger than 12 and being principal to lewd and lascivious behavior on a child younger than 16. He was sentenced to eight years of probation.

Morrissey was set to sue UK music weekly the NME after it failed to apologise for an article focusing on his views on immigration. The magazine had criticised the 48 year old singer and former Smiths star for allegedly telling a reporter Britain had lost its identity due to high levels of immigration.

Control, the biopic about late Joy Division singer Ian Curtis scooped five prizes at the British Independent Film Awards. The black-and-white film, which featured The Killers, David Bowie and New Order on the soundtrack, was shot for just £3m.

Pop Idol creator Simon Fuller dropped his £100m copyright case against the X Factor's Simon Cowell after Fuller settled the case out of court in a deal which made him a joint partner in the X Factor show. Mr Fuller had claimed Mr Cowell's ITV talent show X Factor copied his successful Pop Idol format, in a case taken to London's High Court. As part of the settlement, Mr Cowell agreed to appear in at least five more series of American Idol.

Three paintings by Sir Paul McCartney were bought for just £35 each at the Secrets Postcard Sale at London's Royal College of Art. Members of the public gambled on whether they were buying works by celebrity artists at a fraction of their value, as a picture's creator was only made known after it has sold.

Beatles guitarist George Harrison died in Los Angeles of lung cancer aged 58. Following the breakup of The Beatles Harrison had a successful career as a solo artist and later as part of the Traveling Wilburys. The youngest member of The Beatles, (aged 16 when he joined), his compositions include ‘Taxman’, ‘Here Comes the Sun’, ‘Something’, and ‘While My Guitar Gently Weeps’. Harrison released the acclaimed triple album, All Things Must Pass, in 1970, from which came the worldwide No.1 single 'My Sweet Lord.'

U2's Larry Mullen came to the rescue of motorcyclist who had been involved in an accident. Larry was driving home when he saw the motorcyclist who had crashed and stopped to call for help on his phone and then waited for the ambulance to arrive.

Chuck Berry's longtime piano player, Johnnie Johnson, sued the rock legend, alleging that he wrote the music for 52 of Berry's classics. The suit was thrown out by a judge who ruled that the statute of limitations had run out on any claims.

American singer and bandleader Curtis Knight died aged 54. Jimi Hendrix had been a member of his band in the 60s. Though Hendrix wasn't in the group very long, he was featured on over 60 songs, 26 studio and 35 live recordings some of which have been released on record.

'Perfect Day' performed by various artists including Elton John, Bono, Tom Jones and David Bowie went to No.1 on the UK singles chart. Originally written and recorded in 1973 by Lou Reed, this new collaboration of 29 major artists was a fundraiser for the BBC Children In Need charity.

Whitney Houston pulled out of a concert sponsored by the Moonies two hours before she was due on stage after finding out the event was a mass wedding for over 1,000 Moonie couple's. The religious group said they had no intention of suing providing the singer returned the $1m fee she had received.

'You Give Love A Bad Name' by Bon Jovi went to No.1 in the US, giving the group their first big hit. It was written by group leaders Jon Bon Jovi and Richie Sambora along with Desmond Child, whose choruses can be heard on 'I Was Made For Lovin' You' by Kiss and 'Dude (Looks Like A Lady)' by Aerosmith. Bon Jovi's next single is 'Livin' On A Prayer,' written by the same trio.

sArtist: Now That's What I Call Music
sBand: Now That's What I Call Music
sDescription: Now That's What I Call Music was launched in the UK with a mission to anthologise the biggest chart hits of the day. The first track on the first album was You Can't Hurry Love by Phil Collins and also contained hits like 'Karma Chameleon', 'Red Red Wine' and 'Total Eclipse Of The Heart'. The series took its name from a 1930s advertising poster for Danish bacon, featuring a pig saying. "Now, That's What I Call Music" as it listened to a chicken singing. The most successful volume to date is 1999's Now That's What I Call Music 44, which sold 2.3 million copies and is the biggest-selling compilation album ever. It opened with Britney Spears' ...Baby One More Time.

John and Yoko's Double Fantasy album was released. Though initially poorly received, the album is notable for its association with Lennon's murder three weeks after its release, whereupon it became a worldwide commercial success, and went on to win the 1981 Album of the Year at the 24th Annual Grammy Awards.
ABBA scored their ninth and last UK No.1 single with 'Super Trouper', the group's 25th Top 40 hit in the UK. The name "Super Trouper" referred to the gigantic spotlights used in stadium concerts.

Lancaster local council cancelled the Sex Pistols gig at Lancaster Poly, England. The reason was given in a statement by the council saying: 'We don't want that sort of filth (The Sex Pistols) in the town limits.'

Neil Young recorded 'Like a Hurricane' at the Broken Arrow Ranch in Woodside, California. The song was released a couple years later on his album American Stars 'n Bars. The song remains a fan favourite and concert staple for the remainder of Young's career.

The Beatles went to No.1 on the US singles chart with their twenty-sixth release in the United States.'Come Together / Something', which became the group's 18th US No.1. Lennon was inspired by Timothy Leary's campaign for governor of California titled "Come together, join the party" against Ronald Reagan giving him the idea for the track. ’Something’ was the first Beatles song written by George Harrison to appear as an A-side.
Colorado Governor John A. Love declared a Rolling Stones day throughout the State as The Stones appeared at The Denver Coliseum in Colorado during a North American tour.
I Want to Hold Your Hand by The Beatles was released in the UK. For the first time in the UK advanced orders passed the million mark before the record was released.

American rapper The Game, (Jayceon Terrell Taylor), who scored the 2005 US No.1 with his debut album, The Documentary. His 2006 follow-up, Doctor's Advocate, received double platinum certification and two Grammy Award nominations, Best Rap Song and Best Rap Performance by a Duo or Group for its single, 'Hate It or Love It' (featuring 50 Cent). In 2011, Game was refused entry to Canada for alleged gang ties in Los Angeles; concert organisers said he was associated with the African American street gang Bloods.

Filipino-American rapper, singer and record producer Apl.De.Ap who with the Black Eyed Peas had the 2003 US & UK No.1 single 'Where Is The Love'. In 2008, he founded the Apl Foundation International (Aplfi) to help various communities and children in the Philippines and throughout Asia.

American musician Keith Carlock who has played drums with Toto, Steely Dan, James Taylor, John Mayer and Sting. In Modern Drummer's 2009 Readers Poll, he was voted best Pop, Fusion, and All-Around drummer.

Martin Carr, guitarist, singer with English alternative rock band The Boo Radleys, who had the 1995 UK No.9 single 'Wake Up Boo'. Their name is taken from the character Boo Radley in Harper Lee's 1960 novel, To Kill a Mockingbird. After the breakup of the Boo Radleys, Carr launched a solo career, taking the name bravecaptain from a song by the US rock band Firehose.

Jonathan Knight, from American boy band New Kids on the Block, who had the 1989 UK No.1 single 'You Got It, The Right Stuff', and the 1990 US No.1 single 'Step By Step'. They enjoyed success in the late 1980s and early 1990s and have sold more than 80 million records worldwide.

Wendy Wu from English new wave the Photos, who had a top 5 album in the UK Albums Chart in 1980. Wu went on to release some  solo singles during 1982 and 1983, and then joined Steve Strange to form the duo Strange Cruise in 1986.

Michael Dempsey, bassist from the English new wave band The Lotus Eaters who had the 1983 UK No.15 single 'First Picture Of You' which was a hit in continental Europe, notably France, Italy, Belgium and Spain. Dempsey has also worked with The Cure and Associates.

Jennifer Batten, American guitarist who has worked as a session musician and solo artist. Batten played in all three of Michael Jackson's world tours, and from 1999 to 2001 she toured and recorded with Jeff Beck.

Australian singer, songwriter, musician and producer Chris Bailey. He was the co-founder and singer of rock band the Saints. Their debut single '(I'm) Stranded' (1976) has been cited as "one of the iconic singles of the era", and pre-dated debuts by contemporary punk acts such as the Sex Pistols, Buzzcocks and The Clash. In 2007, Australian Musician magazine voted this the fourth most significant moment in the history of Australian pop/rock. Bailey died on 9 April 2022, aged 65.

Barry Goudreau, guitar, Boston, (1977 UK No.22 single 'More Than A Feeling', 1986 US No.1 single 'Amanda'). Boston have sold more than 75 million records worldwide, including 31 million albums in the United States, of which 17 million were from their self-titled debut album and seven million were for their second album, Don't Look Back, making them one of the world's best-selling artists.

Roger Troutman, American composer, songwriter, producer, multi-instrumentalist and the founder of the band Zapp who helped spearhead the funk movement and heavily influenced west coast hip hop due to the scene's heavy sampling of his music over the years. Troutman was found shot and critically wounded outside his northwest Dayton recording studio on 25th April 1999.

American musician and guitarist  Ronnie Montrose, who was a member of Montrose (Montrose's 1973 debut album has often been cited as "America's answer to Led Zeppelin"), and the Edgar Winter Group, who had the 1973 US No.1 & UK No.18 single 'Frankenstein'. He worked with many other artists as a session musician. He died on 3 March 2012 from a self-inflicted gunshot wound after taking his own life age 64.

Felix Cavaliere, keyboards, with American rock band, The Rascals (initially known as The Young Rascals) who had the US No.1 hits 'Good Lovin'' (1966), 'Groovin'' (1967), and 'People Got to Be Free' (1968).

English drummer, singer and songwriter Twink (John Alder), who was a central figure in the English psychedelic movement. He was a member of The Pretty Things and The Pink Fairies. In 1967, Twink recorded with a group called Santa Barbara Machine Head. It featured Ronnie Wood, Kim Gardner (later of Ashton, Gardner & Dyke) and keyboardist Jon Lord (later of Deep Purple). Twink converted to Islam and changed his name to Mohammed Abdullah.

Tim Davis American drummer, singer and songwriter, who co-founded the Steve Miller Band who had the 1974 US No.1 & 1990 UK No.1 single 'The Joker', the 1976 hit 'Fly Like an Eagle' and the 1982 US No.1 hit 'Abracadabra'. 
He died on 20 September 1988 age 44.

American singer Jody Miller. She had commercial success in the genres of country, folk and pop and became the second female artist to win a country music accolade from the Grammy Awards, which came off the success of her 1965 song 'Queen of the House' which was an answer song to Roger Miller's 'King of the Road'. Miller died on October 6, 2022 age 80.

Denny Doherty, from American folk rock vocal group The Mamas & the Papas who had the 1965 hit 'California Dreamin'', the 1966 US No.1 single 'Monday Monday' and the 1967 hit 'Dedicated to the One I Love'. Doherty died on 19th Jan 2007 at the age of 66 after a short illness. Doherty started his musical career in 1956 with a band called the Hepsters and in 1963, established a friendship with Cass Elliot when she was with a band called The Big 3.
American flugelhorn player, trumpeter and composer Chuck Mangione, who had the 1978 US No.4 single, 'Feels So Good'. Mangione died in his sleep at his Rochester home on July 22, 2025, age 84.

American record producer and musician, Meco Monardo, who had the 1977 US No.1 & UK No.7 single 'Star Wars Theme'. As a session musician, he played the trombone with acts like Diana Ross. He performed on Diana Ross' 1980 album Diana as a favour to producer (and neighbour) Nile Rodgers. His solo on the single 'I'm Coming Out' is notable because of the rarity of trombone features on post-big-band era pop records.

English blues and rock musician, songwriter and producer John Mayall, the 'father of the UK blues movement'. His Bluesbreakers Band has featured Eric Clapton Mick Taylor, Mick Fleetwood, John McVie, Jack Bruce, Peter Green and Jimmy McCulloch. He had a career that spanned nearly seven decades, remaining an active musician until his death. Mayall died at his home in California on 22 July 2024, at the age of 90.

Country singer and songwriter Merle Travis. He is best known for his unique guitar style, which is still referred to as Travis picking among guitarists. He wrote 'Sixteen Tons', a 1955 US No.1 for Ernie Ford. He was inducted into the Nashville Songwriters Hall of Fame in 1970 and elected to the Country Music Hall of Fame in 1977. Travis died of a heart attack at his Tahlequah, Oklahoma, home on 20th October 1983.
